title: Precedent: agents and inboxes
summary: How an agent asks, and how you clear what it asked. What each does, and what we'd borrow (the cards that borrow it are in brackets).

checks.text: Linear agents: A session is pending, active, awaiting input, errored or complete; asking you something is an elicitation. We borrow: a card is an elicitation, and the agent's state drives every badge (Can Switchboard tell when the ag…; Each project shows what its agen…)
Linear Inbox and Triage: J and K to move, number keys for outcomes, snooze that wakes early. We borrow: review mode's keys (Review mode: one card at a time,…)
Superhuman: One inbox split by what matters, worked through in one sitting. We borrow: one Boards window across every project (One Boards window for every proj…)
GitHub notifications: Every notification says why it's there; Done keeps it findable. We borrow: reason labels, and the Record (Every card says why it's there; Decided cards: take them off, or…)
HEY Screener: New senders wait once; your choice sticks. We borrow: the wishlist as a screener (The wishlist as a screener)
Claude Code hooks: permission_prompt and idle_prompt fire when the agent waits. We borrow: the quiet "waiting" dot (Can Switchboard tell when the ag…)

why: Each is a shipped product solving the same problem we have: something asks you, and you clear it fast. Linear's agent states are the closest match to an agent that waits on you.

options.label: Looks right
options.then: Keep these as the models the cards cite, and build to them.
